# Background

This document analyses mutant feedback experiments testing plant growth responses to BXplus- and BXminus-conditioned soil microbiomes.

For the \*mmf1\* mutant screen, three experiments are shown individually in detail:

\- E-III: \*mmf1\* repetition 1

\- E-IV: \*mmf1\* repetition 2

\- E-V: \*mmf1\* repetition 3

A final combined \*mmf1\* analysis is then performed using pre-combined tabs in \`Dataset4\`, which include five experiments in total.

For the ETI mutant screen, one experiment is shown individually in detail:

\- E-VI: ETI mutants

A final combined ETI analysis is then performed using pre-combined tabs in \`Dataset4\`, which include four experiments in total.

The \*mmf1\* complementation lines are analysed separately as:

\- E-X: \*mmf1\* complementation lines

# Experiment overview

| Experiment | Description | Soil batch | Notes |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| E-III | *mmf1* repetition 1 | BS04 | Growth |
| E-IV | *mmf1* repetition 2 | BS04 | Growth, microbiota, transcriptome |
| E-V | *mmf1* repetition 3 | BS09 | Growth |
| E-VI | ETI mutants | BS07 | Growth |
| E-VII | ETI mutants | BS07 | Growth |
| E-VIII | ETI mutants | BS11 | Growth, transcriptome |
| E-IX | ETI mutants | BS10 | Growth |
| E-X | *mmf1* complementation lines | BS10 | Growth |

## Helper function

```{r}
#| label: helper-functions
#| echo: false
# --- PUBLICATION FIGURE REFERENCE ------------------------------------------
# Supports: Fig. 4b
#   Shared plotting and statistics helpers
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Pick the first existing sheet from a list of candidates.
pick_sheet <- function(candidates, available = all_sheets) {
  hit <- candidates[candidates %in% available][1]
  if (is.na(hit)) {
    stop(
      "None of these candidate sheet names were found:\n",
      paste(candidates, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }
  hit
}

# Standardize BX and line factors.
standardise_groups <- function(df, line_levels = NULL) {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
    )

  if (!is.null(line_levels)) {
    df <- df %>%
      mutate(line = factor(line, levels = line_levels))
  }

  df
}

# Calculate simple per-line means and delta = plus - minus.
delta_means <- function(data, response) {
  data %>%
    group_by(line, BX) %>%
    summarise(mean_value = mean(.data[[response]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = BX, values_from = mean_value) %>%
    mutate(delta_plus_minus = plus - minus)
}

# One-way ANOVA within each genotype/line for BX effect + FDR correction across lines.
bx_tests_by_line <- function(data, response) {
  data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[response]]), !is.na(line), !is.na(BX)) %>%
    group_by(line) %>%
    summarise(
      p_value = summary(aov(stats::as.formula(paste(response, "~ BX")), data = cur_data()))[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1],
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "fdr"),
      significance = cut(
        p_adj,
        breaks = c(0, 1e-04, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
        labels = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "ns"),
        include.lowest = TRUE
      )
    )
}

# Z-score within experiment for combined plots.
zscore_within_experiment <- function(data, response, experiment_var = "experiment", new_name) {
  data %>%
    group_by(.data[[experiment_var]]) %>%
    mutate("{new_name}" := as.numeric(scale(.data[[response]]))) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Standard single-experiment boxplot.
make_single_plot <- function(data,
                             y_var,
                             y_lab,
                             plot_title,
                             x_labels,
                             y_limits,
                             label_y = NULL) {
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = line, y = .data[[y_var]], fill = BX)) +
    geom_boxplot(
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.85),
      alpha = 0.6,
      color = "grey35",
      outlier.colour = NA,
      size = 0.5
    ) +
    ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(
      dodge.width = 0.85,
      size = 1,
      shape = 21,
      color = "black",
      width = 0.1,
      alpha = 0.4,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    stat_summary(
      fun.data = mean_se,
      geom = "errorbar",
      linewidth = 0.5,
      width = 0.4,
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.85)
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Conditioning", values = c("seagreen", "gold2")) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits) +
    ggtitle(plot_title) +
    ylab(y_lab) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = x_labels) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )

  if (!is.null(label_y)) {
    p <- p +
      stat_compare_means(
        method = "t.test",
        paired = FALSE,
        size = 2,
        label.y = label_y,
        label.x = 1
      )
  }

  p
}

# Combined plot for z-scored data with experiment shapes + ΔEMM labels.
make_combined_plot <- function(data,
                               y_var,
                               y_lab,
                               plot_title,
                               x_labels,
                               shape_var,
                               y_limits,
                               p_table,
                               text_y,
                               shape_values = c(21, 22, 23, 24, 25)) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = line, y = .data[[y_var]], fill = BX)) +
    geom_boxplot(
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.85),
      alpha = 0.6,
      color = "grey35",
      outlier.colour = NA,
      size = 0.5
    ) +
    ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(
      aes(shape = .data[[shape_var]], group = interaction(line, BX)),
      dodge.width = 0.85,
      size = 1,
      color = "black",
      width = 0.1,
      alpha = 0.4,
      show.legend = TRUE
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(
      data = p_table,
      aes(x = line, y = text_y, label = label),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 3,
      lineheight = 0.9
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Conditioning", values = c("seagreen", "gold2")) +
    scale_shape_manual(name = "Experiment", values = shape_values) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits) +
    ggtitle(plot_title) +
    ylab(y_lab) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = x_labels) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

# LMM + EMM workflow for combined analyses.
run_lmm_emm <- function(data, response, experiment_var) {
  formula_lmm <- stats::as.formula(
    paste(response, "~ BX * line + (1 |", experiment_var, ")")
  )

  model <- lmer(formula_lmm, data = data)

  emm_BX_by_line <- emmeans(model, ~ BX | line)

  effects_by_line <- pairs(emm_BX_by_line, reverse = TRUE) %>%
    summary(infer = TRUE, adjust = "none") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rename(
      effect_plus_minus = estimate,
      t = t.ratio,
      p = p.value
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      effect_plus_minus = round(effect_plus_minus, 3),
      SE = round(SE, 3),
      lower.CL = round(lower.CL, 3),
      upper.CL = round(upper.CL, 3),
      p = signif(p, 3)
    )

  emm_line_x_BX <- emmeans(model, ~ BX * line)

  diff_in_diff_vs_WT <- contrast(
    emm_line_x_BX,
    interaction = c("revpairwise", "trt.vs.ctrl")
  ) %>%
    summary(infer = TRUE, adjust = "holm") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rename(
      diff_vs_WT = estimate,
      t = t.ratio,
      p_adj = p.value
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      diff_vs_WT = round(diff_vs_WT, 3),
      SE = round(SE, 3),
      lower.CL = round(lower.CL, 3),
      upper.CL = round(upper.CL, 3),
      p_adj = signif(p_adj, 3)
    )

  list(
    model = model,
    effects_by_line = effects_by_line,
    diff_in_diff_vs_WT = diff_in_diff_vs_WT
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: import-data

# -----------------------------

weight_EIV <- read_excel(data_file, sheet = "ExpIV_mmf1_weight") %>%
  mutate(experiment = "E-IV")

weight_EV <- read_excel(data_file, sheet = "ExpV_mmf1_weight") %>%
  mutate(experiment = "E-V")

area_EV <- read_excel(data_file, sheet = "ExpV_mmf1_area") %>%

# -----------------------------

area_EVI <- read_excel(data_file, sheet = "ExpVI_ETI_area") %>%
```

## Factoring and cleaning data

```{r}
#| label: factor-and-cleaning
#| echo: false

bx_levels <- c("minus", "plus")

# mmf1 individual
weight_EIII <- weight_EIII %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(fresh_weight))

area_EIII <- area_EIII %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(plant_region_area))

weight_EIV <- weight_EIV %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1", "mmf1-2")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(fresh_weight))

area_EIV <- area_EIV %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1", "mmf1-2")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(plant_region_area))

weight_EV <- weight_EV %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1", "mmf1-2")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(fresh_weight))

area_EV <- area_EV %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1", "mmf1-2")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(plant_region_area))

# ETI individual
weight_EVI <- weight_EVI %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "eds1", "pad4", "sag101")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
  )

area_EVI <- area_EVI %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "eds1", "pad4", "sag101")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
  )

# complementation
compl_lines_EX <- compl_lines_EX %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-2", "mmf1-2*Nos4-4", "mmf1-2*Nos5-1")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels)
  )

# combined mmf1
plant_weight_comb_mmf1 <- plant_weight_comb_mmf1 %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1", "mmf1-2")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels),
    experiment = factor(exp)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(fresh_weight))

rosette_area_comb_mmf1 <- rosette_area_comb_mmf1 %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1", "mmf1-2")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels),
    experiment = factor(experiment)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(plant_region_area))

# combined ETI
plant_weight_comb_ETI <- plant_weight_comb_ETI %>%
  filter(line != "mmf1-2") %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "eds1", "pad4", "sag101")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels),
    experiment = factor(experiment)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(fresh_weight))

plant_area_comb_ETI <- plant_area_comb_ETI %>%
  filter(line != "mmf1-2") %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "eds1", "pad4", "sag101")),
    BX = factor(BX, levels = bx_levels),
    experiment = factor(experiment)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(plant_region_area))
```

### Statistics

```{r}
#| label: stats-EIII
#| echo: false

anova_fw_EIII <- summary(aov(fresh_weight ~ line * BX, data = weight_EIII))[[1]]
anova_area_EIII <- summary(aov(plant_region_area ~ line * BX, data = area_EIII))[[1]]

kable(anova_fw_EIII, caption = "ANOVA table for fresh weight (E-III)")
kable(anova_area_EIII, caption = "ANOVA table for rosette area (E-III)")

kable(
  bx_tests_by_line(weight_EIII, "fresh_weight"),
  caption = "Per-line BX effect with FDR correction for fresh weight (E-III)"
)

kable(
  bx_tests_by_line(area_EIII, "plant_region_area"),
  caption = "Per-line BX effect with FDR correction for rosette area (E-III)"
)

```

```{r}
  table(plant_weight_comb_ETI$BX, plant_weight_comb_ETI$line),
  caption = "Number of replicates - weight (ETI combined, E-VI to E-IX)"
)

  table(plant_area_comb_ETI$BX, plant_area_comb_ETI$line),
  caption = "Number of replicates - plant area (ETI combined, E-VI to E-IX)"
)
```

### LMM and EMM: fresh weight

```{r}
#| label: lmm-eti-fw
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: |
#|   Extended Data Figure 6c (fresh weight) | Growth feedback in a BXplus microbiome remains intact
#|   in effector-triggered immunity signalling mutants. (a) Phenotypes of 6-week-old WT, and mutants
#|   (eds1-12, pad4-1 and sag101-3) affected in effector-triggered immunity signalling pathways grown
#|   on the BXminus and BXplus soils. Scale bar, 2 cm. (b) Z-score--transformed fresh weight and
#|   rosette area of WT, eds1-12, pad4-1, and sag101-3 plants across four independent experiments
#|   illustrate the positive growth feedback on the BXplus soil microbiome. Values were
#|   z-score--transformed within experiment to account for between-experiment variation. Each point
#|   is an individual plant grown in its own pot, i.e. a biological replicate; number of replicates
#|   is given below each plot. Boxplots show the median (centre line) and the 25th and 75th
#|   percentiles (box bounds); whiskers extend to the most extreme value within 1.5 × the
#|   interquartile range of the nearest box bound, and all plants are plotted as points. The
#|   statistics above the plots are estimated marginal mean (EMM) contrasts of the BX effect within
#|   each genotype (ΔEMM = BXplus − BXminus), computed from a linear mixed-effects model with
#|   experiment as a random intercept to account for variation between experiments. Each ΔEMM is a
#|   two-sided t-test on the estimated marginal means (emmeans). ΔEMM is therefore expressed in the
#|   units of the measurement, not in z-score units. (c) Summary of the same linear mixed-effects
#|   model in (b). For each genotype, the BX effect is reported as the EMM contrast Δ(BXplus −
#|   BXminus) with unadjusted two-sided P values. The table also reports interaction contrasts
#|   relative to WT (ΔΔ vs WT = Δ_mutant − Δ_WT), which test whether the BX response of each mutant
#|   differs from that of WT; these three comparisons form one family per measure and are two-sided
#|   t-tests with Holm adjusted P values. Data are from Dataset 4.
# --- PUBLICATION FIGURE REFERENCE ------------------------------------------
# Produces: Extended Data Fig. 6c
#   LMM summary, ETI mutants fresh weight
#   -> (table printed in the document)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plant_weight_comb_ETI <- plant_weight_comb_ETI %>%
  mutate(
    BX = factor(BX, levels = c("minus", "plus")),
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "eds1", "pad4", "sag101")),
    experiment = factor(experiment)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(fresh_weight))

# Fit model first
eti_fw_lmm <- run_lmm_emm(
  data = plant_weight_comb_ETI,
  response = "fresh_weight",
  experiment_var = "experiment"
)

# Inspect model
summary(eti_fw_lmm$model)

# Within-line BX effect
kable(
  eti_fw_lmm$effects_by_line,
  caption = "Within-line ΔEMM = BXplus - BXminus for ETI fresh weight"
)

# Difference-in-differences vs WT
kable(
  eti_fw_lmm$diff_in_diff_vs_WT,
  caption = "Difference-in-differences relative to WT for ETI fresh weight"
)

# Mutant vs WT within each BX condition
emm_line_by_BX <- emmeans(eti_fw_lmm$model, ~ line | BX)

line_vs_WT_by_BX <- contrast(
  emm_line_by_BX,
  method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
  ref = "WT",
  adjust = "holm"
) %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    lower.CL = round(lower.CL, 3),
    upper.CL = round(upper.CL, 3),
    p.value = signif(p.value, 3)
  )

kable(
  line_vs_WT_by_BX,
  caption = "Mutant vs WT contrasts within each BX condition for ETI fresh weight (Holm-adjusted)"
)
```

### Plot combined ETI fresh weight

```{r}
#| label: fig-eti-fw-combined
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: |

#|   in effector-triggered immunity signalling mutants. (a) Phenotypes of 6-week-old WT, and mutants
#|   (eds1-12, pad4-1 and sag101-3) affected in effector-triggered immunity signalling pathways grown

# --- PUBLICATION FIGURE REFERENCE ------------------------------------------
# Produces: Extended Data Fig. 6b

# ------------------------------------------------------------

plant_weight_comb_ETI_z <- zscore_within_experiment(
  plant_weight_comb_ETI,

p_table_eti_fw <- eti_fw_lmm$effects_by_line %>%

  )

plot_ETI_fw_combined <- make_combined_plot(
```

### LMM and EMM: rosette area

### Plot combined ETI rosette area

```{r}
#| label: fig-eti-area-combined
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: |
#|   Extended Data Figure 6b (rosette area) | Growth feedback in a BXplus microbiome remains intact
#|   in effector-triggered immunity signalling mutants. (a) Phenotypes of 6-week-old WT, and mutants
#|   (eds1-12, pad4-1 and sag101-3) affected in effector-triggered immunity signalling pathways grown
#|   on the BXminus and BXplus soils. Scale bar, 2 cm. (b) Z-score--transformed fresh weight and
#|   rosette area of WT, eds1-12, pad4-1, and sag101-3 plants across four independent experiments
#|   illustrate the positive growth feedback on the BXplus soil microbiome. Values were
#|   z-score--transformed within experiment to account for between-experiment variation. Each point
#|   is an individual plant grown in its own pot, i.e. a biological replicate; number of replicates
#|   is given below each plot. Boxplots show the median (centre line) and the 25th and 75th
#|   percentiles (box bounds); whiskers extend to the most extreme value within 1.5 × the
#|   interquartile range of the nearest box bound, and all plants are plotted as points. The
#|   statistics above the plots are estimated marginal mean (EMM) contrasts of the BX effect within
#|   each genotype (ΔEMM = BXplus − BXminus), computed from a linear mixed-effects model with
#|   experiment as a random intercept to account for variation between experiments. Each ΔEMM is a
#|   two-sided t-test on the estimated marginal means (emmeans). ΔEMM is therefore expressed in the
#|   units of the measurement, not in z-score units. (c) Summary of the same linear mixed-effects
#|   model in (b). For each genotype, the BX effect is reported as the EMM contrast Δ(BXplus −
#|   BXminus) with unadjusted two-sided P values. The table also reports interaction contrasts
#|   relative to WT (ΔΔ vs WT = Δ_mutant − Δ_WT), which test whether the BX response of each mutant
#|   differs from that of WT; these three comparisons form one family per measure and are two-sided
#|   t-tests with Holm adjusted P values. Data are from Dataset 4.
# --- PUBLICATION FIGURE REFERENCE ------------------------------------------
```

### **LMM and EMM: fresh weight**

```{r}
#| label: lmm-mmf1-fw
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: |
#|   Extended Data Figure 5b (fresh weight) | Growth feedback in a BXplus microbiome is consistently
#|   lost in mmf1 mutants. (a and b) Repeated growth feedbacks (Experiment III - V, VIII, IX and X)
#|   of Col-0 wild type (WT) and two mmf1 T-DNA insertion mutants (At3g44630) grown on the BXminus
#|   and BXplus soil microbiomes. Feedback experiments were performed on greenhouse-conditioned soil
#|   batches BS04 (Experiment III and IV), BS09 (V and X), BS10 (IX) and BS11 (VIII). (a)
#|   Z-score--transformed fresh weight and rosette area of WT and mmf1 mutants across six independent
#|   experiments. WT was present in all six experiments, mmf1-1 in three and mmf1-2 in five. Values
#|   were z-score--transformed within experiment to account for between-experiment variation. Each
#|   point is an individual plant grown in its own pot, i.e. a biological replicate; number of
#|   replicates is given below each plot. Boxplots show the median (centre line) and the 25th and
#|   75th percentiles (box bounds); whiskers extend to the most extreme value within 1.5 × the
#|   interquartile range of the nearest box bound, and all plants are plotted as points. The
#|   statistics above the plots are estimated marginal mean (EMM) contrasts of the BX effect within
#|   each genotype (ΔEMM = BXplus − BXminus), computed from a linear mixed-effects model with
#|   experiment as a random intercept to account for variation between experiments. Each ΔEMM is a
#|   two-sided t-test on the estimated marginal means (emmeans). ΔEMM is therefore expressed in the
#|   units of the measurement, not in z-score units. (b) Summary of the same linear mixed-effects
#|   model in (a). For each genotype, the BX effect is reported as the EMM contrast Δ(BXplus −
#|   BXminus) with unadjusted two-sided P values. The table also reports interaction contrasts
#|   relative to WT (ΔΔ vs WT = Δ_mutant − Δ_WT), which test whether the BX response of each mutant
#|   differs from that of WT; these two comparisons form one family per measure and are two-sided
#|   t-tests with Holm adjusted P values. Data are from Dataset 4.
# --- PUBLICATION FIGURE REFERENCE ------------------------------------------
# Produces: Extended Data Fig. 5b
#   LMM summary, fresh weight (experiment as random intercept)
#   -> (table printed in the document)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------
# mmf1 pooled fresh weight analysis
# keeps plant_weight_comb_mmf1 for downstream plotting
# -----------------------------

# 1) Prepare data once
plant_weight_comb_mmf1 <- plant_weight_comb_mmf1 %>%
  mutate(
    BX = factor(BX, levels = c("minus", "plus")),
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1", "mmf1-2")),
    experiment = factor(exp)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(fresh_weight))

# 2) Fit one mixed model
mmf1_fw_lmm <- run_lmm_emm(
  data = plant_weight_comb_mmf1,
  response = "fresh_weight",
  experiment_var = "experiment"
)

# 3) Inspect model
summary(mmf1_fw_lmm$model)

# -----------------------------
# A. Within-line BX effect
#    ΔEMM = BXplus - BXminus
# -----------------------------
kable(
  mmf1_fw_lmm$effects_by_line,
  caption = "Within-line ΔEMM = BXplus - BXminus for mmf1 fresh weight"
)

# -----------------------------
# B. Difference-in-differences vs WT
# -----------------------------
kable(
  mmf1_fw_lmm$diff_in_diff_vs_WT,
  caption = "Difference-in-differences relative to WT for mmf1 fresh weight"
)

# -----------------------------
# C. Mutant vs WT within each BX condition
# -----------------------------
emm_line_by_BX_mmf1 <- emmeans(mmf1_fw_lmm$model, ~ line | BX)

line_vs_WT_by_BX_mmf1 <- contrast(
  emm_line_by_BX_mmf1,
  method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
  ref = "WT",
  adjust = "holm"
) %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    lower.CL = round(lower.CL, 3),
    upper.CL = round(upper.CL, 3),
    p.value = signif(p.value, 3)
  )

kable(
  line_vs_WT_by_BX_mmf1,
  caption = "Mutant vs WT contrasts within each BX condition for mmf1 fresh weight (Holm-adjusted)"
)

# -----------------------------
# D. Estimated marginal means for line
#    averaged across BX conditions
# -----------------------------
emm_line_mmf1_fw <- emmeans(mmf1_fw_lmm$model, ~ line)

emm_line_mmf1_fw_table <- summary(emm_line_mmf1_fw) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    emmean = round(emmean, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    lower.CL = round(lower.CL, 3),
    upper.CL = round(upper.CL, 3)
  )

kable(
  emm_line_mmf1_fw_table,
  caption = "Estimated marginal means for mmf1 fresh weight by line, averaged across BX conditions (experiment included as a random intercept)"
)

# -----------------------------
# E. Mutant vs WT averaged across BX conditions
# -----------------------------
line_vs_WT_mmf1_fw <- contrast(
  emm_line_mmf1_fw,
  method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
  ref = "WT",
  adjust = "holm"
) %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(
    diff_EMM = estimate,
    t = t.ratio,
    p = p.value
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    diff_EMM = round(diff_EMM, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    lower.CL = round(lower.CL, 3),
    upper.CL = round(upper.CL, 3),
    p = signif(p, 3)
  )

kable(
  line_vs_WT_mmf1_fw,
  caption = "Mutant vs WT contrasts for mmf1 fresh weight, averaged across BX conditions and corrected for experiment (Holm-adjusted)"
)

# -----------------------------
# F. All line × BX combinations relative to WT in BXminus
#    Uses the same mixed model, so experiment is still accounted for
# -----------------------------
emm_line_BX_mmf1_fw <- emmeans(mmf1_fw_lmm$model, ~ line * BX)

emm_line_BX_mmf1_fw_table <- summary(emm_line_BX_mmf1_fw) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    emmean = round(emmean, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    lower.CL = round(lower.CL, 3),
    upper.CL = round(upper.CL, 3)
  )

kable(
  emm_line_BX_mmf1_fw_table,
  caption = "Estimated marginal means for mmf1 fresh weight by line and BX condition (experiment included as a random intercept)"
)

# Check that row 1 is WT in BXminus
emm_line_BX_mmf1_fw_table

vs_WTminus_mmf1_fw <- contrast(
  emm_line_BX_mmf1_fw,
  method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
  ref = 1,
  adjust = "holm"
) %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(
    diff_vs_WTminus = estimate,
    t = t.ratio,
    p = p.value
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    diff_vs_WTminus = round(diff_vs_WTminus, 3),
    SE = round(SE, 3),
    lower.CL = round(lower.CL, 3),
    upper.CL = round(upper.CL, 3),
    p = signif(p, 3)
  )

kable(
  vs_WTminus_mmf1_fw,
  caption = "Fresh weight contrasts relative to WT in BXminus soil for mmf1 lines (experiment included as a random intercept; Holm-adjusted)"
)
```

```{r}
#|   each genotype (ΔEMM = BXplus − BXminus), computed from a linear mixed-effects model with
#|   experiment as a random intercept to account for variation between experiments. Each ΔEMM is a
#|   two-sided t-test on the estimated marginal means (emmeans). ΔEMM is therefore expressed in the
#|   units of the measurement, not in z-score units. (b) Summary of the same linear mixed-effects
#|   model in (a). For each genotype, the BX effect is reported as the EMM contrast Δ(BXplus −
#|   BXminus) with unadjusted two-sided P values. The table also reports interaction contrasts
#|   relative to WT (ΔΔ vs WT = Δ_mutant − Δ_WT), which test whether the BX response of each mutant
#|   differs from that of WT; these two comparisons form one family per measure and are two-sided
#|   t-tests with Holm adjusted P values. Data are from Dataset 4.
# --- PUBLICATION FIGURE REFERENCE ------------------------------------------
# Produces: Extended Data Fig. 5a
#   Z-scored rosette area, WT vs mmf1 across experiments
#   -> Output/figures/mmf1_mutants_area_comb_zscore.pdf
# ------------------------------------------------------------

rosette_area_comb_mmf1_z <- zscore_within_experiment(
  rosette_area_comb_mmf1,
  response = "plant_region_area",
  experiment_var = "experiment",
  new_name = "plant_area_z"
)

p_table_mmf1_area <- mmf1_area_lmm$effects_by_line %>%
  mutate(
    line = factor(line, levels = c("WT", "mmf1-1", "mmf1-2")),
    label = paste0("ΔEMM = ", effect_plus_minus, "\n", "p = ", p)
  )

plot_mmf1_area_combined <- make_combined_plot(
  data = rosette_area_comb_mmf1_z,
  y_var = "plant_area_z",
  y_lab = "Rosette area (z-score per experiment)",
  plot_title = "mmf1 - Rosette area",
  x_labels = c("WT", expression(italic("mmf1-1")), expression(italic("mmf1-2"))),
  shape_var = "experiment",
  y_limits = c(-3, 4),
  p_table = p_table_mmf1_area,
  text_y = 4,
  shape_values = c(21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 8)
)

plot_mmf1_area_combined

ggsave(
  filename = "mmf1_mutants_area_comb_zscore.pdf", 
  plot = plot_mmf1_area_combined, 
  width = 10, 
  height = 11, 
  units = "cm", 
  path = "Output/figures/"
)
```
#Export Source Data

```{r}
#| label: Source Data
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| paged-print: false
## ---- Source data export: Extended Data Fig. 5 --------------------------------
## Run after the ED Fig. 5 objects exist, i.e. after the chunks that create
##   plant_weight_comb_mmf1_z, rosette_area_comb_mmf1_z   (panel a)
##   mmf1_fw_lmm, mmf1_area_lmm                           (panel b)
## Re-run those chunks first if you have changed the input data, so that the
## z-scores and the model contrasts both come from the cleaned samples.

library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)

OUT <- "Output/Tables/Source_Data_Extended_Data_Fig5.xlsx"

## ---- panel (a): one row per plotted point ------------------------------------
## measured value and the z-score that is actually plotted, both kept.
panel_a <- function(df, value_col, z_col, rep_col = "number", label_col = "exp") {
  stopifnot(all(c("line", "condition", "BX", rep_col, "experiment",
                  value_col, z_col) %in% names(df)))
  out <- df %>%
    transmute(genotype   = as.character(line),
              condition  = as.character(condition),
              microbiome = as.character(BX),
              replicate  = .data[[rep_col]],
              experiment = experiment,
              experiment_label = if (label_col %in% names(df)) as.character(.data[[label_col]]) else NA_character_,
              !!value_col := .data[[value_col]],
              !!z_col     := .data[[z_col]]) %>%
    arrange(experiment, genotype, microbiome, replicate)
  if (all(is.na(out$experiment_label))) out$experiment_label <- NULL
  out
}

fw_sheet   <- panel_a(plant_weight_comb_mmf1_z, "fresh_weight",      "fresh_weight_z")
area_sheet <- panel_a(rosette_area_comb_mmf1_z, "plant_region_area", "plant_area_z")

## ---- panel (b): both contrast families from the fitted models ----------------
contrasts_of <- function(lmm, measure) {
  within_genotype <- lmm$effects_by_line %>%
    transmute(measure,
              contrast_type = "BX effect within genotype",
              genotype = as.character(line),
              contrast = as.character(contrast),
              estimate = effect_plus_minus, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL,
              t_ratio = t, p_value = p)

  dd <- lmm$diff_in_diff_vs_WT
  line_col <- grep("^line", names(dd), value = TRUE)[1]   # line_trt.vs.ctrl
  bx_col   <- grep("^BX",   names(dd), value = TRUE)[1]   # BX_revpairwise

  vs_wt <- dd %>%
    transmute(measure,
              contrast_type = "genotype x BX interaction vs WT",
              genotype = sub(" - WT$", "", as.character(.data[[line_col]])),
              contrast = paste0("(", .data[[bx_col]], ") in ", .data[[line_col]]),
              estimate = diff_vs_WT, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL,
              t_ratio = t, p_value = p_adj)

  bind_rows(within_genotype, vs_wt)
}

lmm_sheet <- bind_rows(contrasts_of(mmf1_fw_lmm,   "fresh weight"),
                       contrasts_of(mmf1_area_lmm, "rosette area"))

## ---- index tab ---------------------------------------------------------------
index <- data.frame(
  Figure      = "Extended Data Fig. 5",
  Panel       = c("a", "a", "b"),
  Description = c("Z-scored fresh weight across experiments",
                  "Z-scored rosette area across experiments",
                  "Linear mixed model contrasts"),
  Worksheet   = c("EDFig5a_fresh_weight_z", "EDFig5a_rosette_area_z",
                  "EDFig5b_LMM_contrasts"),
  `Source data` = c(
    rep("Both the measured value and the z-score that is plotted are given. One row per plant.", 2),
    paste("Model: response ~ BX * line + (1 | experiment), fitted on the measured values.",
          "BX effect within genotype: unadjusted. Interaction vs WT: Holm-adjusted within measure.",
          "Two-sided t-tests, Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom.")),
  check.names = FALSE)

## ---- checks ------------------------------------------------------------------
## the exported z must be the z that was plotted: within each experiment it is
## centred, so the mean is zero. a non-zero mean means the frame was z-scored
## before the samples were dropped.
zmeans <- c(tapply(fw_sheet$fresh_weight_z,  fw_sheet$experiment,   mean, na.rm = TRUE),
            tapply(area_sheet$plant_area_z,  area_sheet$experiment, mean, na.rm = TRUE))
if (max(abs(zmeans)) > 1e-6)
  warning("z-scores are not centred within experiment - re-run the z-scoring after cleaning")

stopifnot(nrow(fw_sheet) > 0, nrow(area_sheet) > 0, nrow(lmm_sheet) > 0,
          !any(duplicated(fw_sheet[c("experiment", "genotype", "microbiome", "replicate")])),
          !any(duplicated(area_sheet[c("experiment", "genotype", "microbiome", "replicate")])))

cat("genotypes:", paste(sort(unique(fw_sheet$genotype)), collapse = ", "),
    "| experiments:", paste(sort(unique(fw_sheet$experiment)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
print(table(fw_sheet$genotype, fw_sheet$microbiome))
print(table(area_sheet$genotype, area_sheet$microbiome))

## ---- write -------------------------------------------------------------------
wb <- createWorkbook()
sheets <- list(Index = index,
               EDFig5a_fresh_weight_z = fw_sheet,
               EDFig5a_rosette_area_z = area_sheet,
               EDFig5b_LMM_contrasts  = lmm_sheet)
for (nm in names(sheets)) {
  d <- sheets[[nm]]
  addWorksheet(wb, nm)
  writeData(wb, nm, d)
  addStyle(wb, nm, createStyle(textDecoration = "bold"), rows = 1, cols = seq_len(ncol(d)))
  freezePane(wb, nm, firstRow = TRUE)
  setColWidths(wb, nm, seq_len(ncol(d)), "auto")
}
saveWorkbook(wb, OUT, overwrite = TRUE)

cat("wrote", OUT, "|", nrow(fw_sheet), "fresh-weight rows,",
    nrow(area_sheet), "rosette-area rows,", nrow(lmm_sheet), "contrasts\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: Source Data ED Fig6
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| paged-print: false
## ---- Source data export: Extended Data Fig. 6 --------------------------------
## Run after the ED Fig. 6 objects exist, i.e. after the chunks that create
##   plant_weight_comb_ETI_z, plant_area_comb_ETI_z   (panel b)
##   eti_fw_lmm, eti_area_lmm                         (panel c)
## Re-run those chunks first if you have changed the input data, so that the
## z-scores and the model contrasts both come from the cleaned samples.

library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)

OUT  <- "Output/Tables/Source_Data_Extended_Data_Fig6.xlsx"
KEYS <- c("experiment", "genotype", "microbiome", "replicate")

## ---- panel (b): one row per plotted point ------------------------------------
## Rows with no measurement (empty pots, NA) are dropped; extra columns such as
## dry_weight are not used as a filter, so a plant weighed fresh but not dry stays.
panel_b <- function(df, value_col, z_col, rep_col = "number",
                    extra = character(), label_col = "exp", drop_na = TRUE) {
  stopifnot(all(c("line", "BX", rep_col, "experiment", value_col, z_col) %in% names(df)))
  extra <- extra[extra %in% names(df)]
  out <- df %>%
    transmute(genotype   = as.character(line),
              microbiome = as.character(BX),
              replicate  = .data[[rep_col]],
              experiment = as.character(experiment),
              experiment_label = if (label_col %in% names(df)) as.character(.data[[label_col]]) else NA_character_,
              !!value_col := .data[[value_col]],
              across(all_of(extra)),
              !!z_col := .data[[z_col]])

  if (drop_na) {
    n0  <- nrow(out)
    out <- filter(out, !is.na(.data[[value_col]]), !is.na(.data[[z_col]]))
    if (n0 > nrow(out))
      message(sprintf("%s: dropped %d row(s) with no %s - empty pots, not exported",
                      z_col, n0 - nrow(out), value_col))
  }

  out <- arrange(out, experiment, genotype, microbiome, replicate)
  if (all(is.na(out$experiment_label))) out$experiment_label <- NULL
  out
}

fw_sheet   <- panel_b(plant_weight_comb_ETI_z, "fresh_weight", "fresh_weight_z",
                      extra = "dry_weight")
area_sheet <- panel_b(plant_area_comb_ETI_z, "plant_region_area", "rosette_area_z")

## ---- panel (c): both contrast families from the fitted models ----------------
contrasts_of <- function(lmm, measure) {
  within_genotype <- lmm$effects_by_line %>%
    transmute(measure,
              contrast_type = "BX effect within genotype",
              genotype = as.character(line),
              contrast = as.character(contrast),
              estimate = effect_plus_minus, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL,
              t_ratio = t, p_value = p)

  dd <- lmm$diff_in_diff_vs_WT
  line_col <- grep("^line", names(dd), value = TRUE)[1]   # line_trt.vs.ctrl
  bx_col   <- grep("^BX",   names(dd), value = TRUE)[1]   # BX_revpairwise

  vs_wt <- dd %>%
    transmute(measure,
              contrast_type = "genotype x BX interaction vs WT",
              genotype = sub(" - WT$", "", as.character(.data[[line_col]])),
              contrast = paste0("(", .data[[bx_col]], ") in ", .data[[line_col]]),
              estimate = diff_vs_WT, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL,
              t_ratio = t, p_value = p_adj)

  bind_rows(within_genotype, vs_wt)
}

lmm_sheet <- bind_rows(contrasts_of(eti_fw_lmm,   "fresh weight"),
                       contrasts_of(eti_area_lmm, "rosette area"))

## ---- index tab ---------------------------------------------------------------
index <- data.frame(
  Figure      = "Extended Data Fig. 6",
  Panel       = c("b", "b", "c", "c"),
  Description = c("Z-scored fresh weight across experiments",
                  "Z-scored rosette area across experiments",
                  "BX effect within genotype",
                  "Genotype x BX interaction contrasts against WT"),
  Worksheet   = c("EDFig6b_fresh_weight_z", "EDFig6b_rosette_area_z",
                  "EDFig6c_LMM_contrasts", "EDFig6c_LMM_contrasts"),
  `Source data` = c(
    "Both the measured value and the z-score that is plotted are given. One row per plant. Dry weight is included where it was recorded.",
    "Both the measured value and the z-score that is plotted are given. One row per plant.",
    "Model: response ~ BX * line + (1 | experiment), fitted on the measured values. Unadjusted two-sided t-tests, Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom.",
    "Same model. Holm-adjusted across the three mutant-versus-WT comparisons within each measure."),
  check.names = FALSE)

## ---- checks ------------------------------------------------------------------
## Rows identical in every column are one plant recorded twice: collapse and say so.
## Rows sharing a key but holding different values are different plants with a bad
## identifier: never merged, only reported.
clean_rows <- function(d, label) {
  n0 <- nrow(d)
  d  <- distinct(d)
  if (n0 > nrow(d))
    message(sprintf("%s: collapsed %d exact duplicate row(s)", label, n0 - nrow(d)))
  k <- d[, KEYS, drop = FALSE]
  clash <- k[duplicated(k) | duplicated(k, fromLast = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(clash)) {
    warning(label, ": ", nrow(unique(clash)),
            " key(s) shared by plants with different values - 'replicate' is not unique, see below")
    print(unique(clash[order(clash$experiment, clash$genotype,
                             clash$microbiome, clash$replicate), ]))
  }
  d
}

fw_sheet   <- clean_rows(fw_sheet,   "EDFig6b_fresh_weight_z")
area_sheet <- clean_rows(area_sheet, "EDFig6b_rosette_area_z")

## the two phenotypes should describe the same plants once empty pots are gone
only_fw   <- anti_join(fw_sheet[KEYS],   area_sheet[KEYS], by = KEYS)
only_area <- anti_join(area_sheet[KEYS], fw_sheet[KEYS],   by = KEYS)
if (nrow(only_fw) || nrow(only_area)) {
  message("plants in fresh weight only: ", nrow(only_fw),
          " | in rosette area only: ", nrow(only_area))
  print(bind_rows(mutate(only_fw,   in_sheet = "fresh weight only"),
                  mutate(only_area, in_sheet = "rosette area only")))
}

## z-scores are centred within experiment; a non-zero mean means the frame was
## z-scored before the samples were cleaned
zmeans <- c(tapply(fw_sheet$fresh_weight_z,   fw_sheet$experiment,   mean, na.rm = TRUE),
            tapply(area_sheet$rosette_area_z, area_sheet$experiment, mean, na.rm = TRUE))
if (max(abs(zmeans)) > 1e-6)
  warning("z-scores are not centred within experiment - re-run the z-scoring after cleaning")

stopifnot(nrow(fw_sheet) > 0, nrow(area_sheet) > 0, nrow(lmm_sheet) > 0)

cat("genotypes:", paste(unique(fw_sheet$genotype), collapse = ", "),
    "| experiments:", paste(sort(unique(fw_sheet$experiment)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
print(table(fw_sheet$genotype,   fw_sheet$microbiome))
print(table(area_sheet$genotype, area_sheet$microbiome))

## ---- write -------------------------------------------------------------------
wb <- createWorkbook()
sheets <- list(Index = index,
               EDFig6b_fresh_weight_z = fw_sheet,
               EDFig6b_rosette_area_z = area_sheet,
               EDFig6c_LMM_contrasts  = lmm_sheet)
for (nm in names(sheets)) {
  d <- sheets[[nm]]
  addWorksheet(wb, nm)
  writeData(wb, nm, d)
  addStyle(wb, nm, createStyle(textDecoration = "bold"), rows = 1, cols = seq_len(ncol(d)))
  freezePane(wb, nm, firstRow = TRUE)
  setColWidths(wb, nm, seq_len(ncol(d)), "auto")
}
saveWorkbook(wb, OUT, overwrite = TRUE)

cat("wrote", OUT, "|", nrow(fw_sheet), "fresh-weight rows,",
    nrow(area_sheet), "rosette-area rows,", nrow(lmm_sheet), "contrasts\n")
```
